name: Unix Timestamp Converter
description: Convert a Unix timestamp to a human-readable date (local time, UTC, and ISO 8601), or a date to a Unix timestamp in seconds or milliseconds.

faq.question: What is a Unix timestamp?
faq.answer: The number of seconds (or, in JavaScript and some other contexts, milliseconds) that have elapsed since January 1, 1970 00:00:00 UTC — the "Unix epoch." It's a timezone-independent way to represent a single moment in time as one number.

faq.question: Why does my timestamp show the wrong date by a factor of 1000?
faq.answer: You most likely have the seconds/milliseconds unit selector set wrong for how the timestamp was generated. Most Unix/server-side tools produce seconds; JavaScript's Date.now() and Date.prototype.getTime() produce milliseconds. Toggling the unit selector should fix a date that looks off by exactly that factor.
